title: Stop catching StateError (an Error subtype) in user_profile_dao.dart's AccountX.accountTier getter
why: `StateError` extends `Error` in dart:core, and `UserTierX.fromDb` throws it specifically for an unrecognized `tier` string — i.e. local DB corruption or a missed enum-value migration. Catching it here and silently returning `UserTier.localBorn` masks that bug: a `cloudBorn` account whose stored tier string ever drifts (bad migration, hand-edited row, future enum rename) silently behaves as local-born everywhere accountTier is read (sync gating, balance-row eligibility per 'Adults never have balance rows (Rule 3)', etc.), with nothing logged.
recommendation: Let the StateError propagate (or catch and rethrow after an AppLogger.error call) instead of returning a silent fallback — an unrecognized tier value is a bug that should be loud, not a normal control-flow case.
acceptance_criteria: AccountX.accountTier no longer has an `on StateError` handler that returns a default value.
A test asserts that an Account row with an unrecognized `tier` string causes accountTier to throw (or to log via AppLogger and rethrow), not silently return localBorn.
